candidate.blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control: follow occupational infection-prevention requirements, bloodborne-pathogen precautions, and employee-exposure safety practices.
candidate.blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — occupational bloodborne-pathogen vaccination
candidate.educational_objective: Recognize the OSHA requirement that hepatitis B vaccination be offered at no cost to employees with occupational blood/OPIM exposure, subject to defined exceptions.

options.D: Hepatitis B vaccine, subject to the standard's stated exceptions.

candidate.rationale: OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1030 requires employers to make hepatitis B vaccine and the vaccination series available to employees with occupational exposure and to provide required medical evaluations/procedures at no cost to the employee. The vaccination must generally be offered after required training and within 10 working days of initial assignment, unless the employee previously completed the series, is demonstrated immune, or the vaccine is medically contraindicated. Therefore D is correct. Influenza, MMR, and Tdap are not the vaccine specifically mandated by the Bloodborne Pathogens Standard for this occupational exposure provision.
candidate.source_claim_supported: OSHA requires hepatitis B vaccination to be made available at no cost to employees with occupational exposure, with specified exceptions for prior vaccination, immunity, or contraindication.
candidate.source_locator: 1910.1030(f)(1)(ii)(A): required evaluations/procedures including hepatitis B vaccine made available at no cost. 1910.1030(f)(2)(i): hepatitis B vaccination offered after training and within 10 working days of initial assignment to employees with occupational exposure unless prior complete series, demonstrated immunity, or medical contraindication.
candidate.stem: A healthcare employee has occupational exposure to blood or other potentially infectious material. Which vaccine must the employer make available at no cost under OSHA's Bloodborne Pathogens Standard?
